__meta__.description: English translations for post processor command.
__meta__.note: The hirarchy in this file is just to make it easier to edit the file, keys named __meta__ and anything under it will not be a part of the translations. This section in the root will be used to get more information of the translations if it is available while other __meta__ keys will be ignored, the rest will be flattened into a key/value pair dictionary and used for translations. This means that keys needs to be unique, otherwise they will overwrite each other. Place any common translations directly in the root so that it is easy to see that they aren't for a specific part.

gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Rotate A-Axis between setu:
When enabled, the A-axis will be rotated to the required position between setups that have different A-axis orientations. This is useful for 4-axis machining where the stock may need to be rotated to access different sides.

This option is only enabled if the selected program has a machine that has an A-axis. It allows the output to be a single file.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP: Retract Y on A-axis rotation: Retract Y axis when rotating A-axis
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Retract Y on A-axis rotati:
When enabled, not only the Z-axis will retract to a safe position before rotating the A-axis but the Y axis will retract as well when rotating between setups. This is useful if the stock in the 4th axis is not round and have potential to collide with the tool when rotating the A-axis.

This option is only enabled if the selected program has a machine that has an A-axis and the option to rotate the A-axis between setups has been selected.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Safe Y-retraction coordina: The Y coordinate to retract to when rotating the A-axis between setups. This coordinate should be set so that the tool will not collide with the stock when retracting to this position.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Tool change code: Allows inserting lines of code before tool changes. For example, you might want M5 (spindle stop), M9 (coolant stop), and/or G28 or G30 (return to home). The code will be placed on the line before the tool change.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: G-codes that mark ending s:
To combine operations generated individually, the ending sequence (which should only appear once) must be found. This entry is the list of G-codes that start this ending sequence.

For example, M30 (end program) would normally be here, but it may not be the first G-code of the ending sequence. M5 (spindle stop), M9 (coolant stop) and G28/G30 (move home) are also candidates, but you should look at the code from your post processor to determine what will work in your case. Either of the G-codes you enter here will mark the start of ending sequence, whichever comes first.

The found sequence that follows, beginning with whichever of these codes that was found first, will be attached at the end of the resulting file(s).
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: G-codes that mark header e:
To separate the header from the body of the program, the ending sequence of the header must be found. This entry is the list of G-codes that mark the end of the header section.

For example, G20 or G21 (set units) would normally be the last code, but it may not always be the case so you can add codes as needed. Look at the code from the post processor to determine what will work in your case.
At the minimum, if nothing is entered here, the tool change code will be used as a marker for ending the header.

The header is assumed to be everything from the start of the program up to and including the line containing whichever of these codes is found last before the tool change (Tn) code or the first G or M code that is not in this list, whichever comes first.

The first header that has been found will be placed at the start of each resulting file. If multiple setups are combined into a single file, only the first header will be used and subsequent headers will be ignored.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Restore rapid moves: Restore rapid (rapid traverse) moves where appropriate. This will find where the movement can be a rapid movement (G0) rather than a cutting move (G1) and change the output so that it rapid movements will be used.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP: Max steps for rapid moves: Maximum steps to count as a rapid move
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Max steps for rapid moves:
To limit the scope in the search for a candidate to swap to a rapid move you can now set the maximum number of program steps to search for the end of the rapid move.

This can be useful if you use the shortest path option when setting type of rapid movements as they can be done using several steps and sometimes it could be quite a few, so if you notice that the rapid moves doesn't work everywhere and you use shortest path as strategy, try increasing this value.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Minimum rapid move distanc: The minimum movement distance to add rapid movements to. To limit the jerkyness of the machine you can set a limit of the shortest distance the machine needs to move to change from a cutting move (G1) to a rapid move (G0).
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Add line numbers: Add line numbers to each line of each output file.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP: Number of line digits: The number of digits to use
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Numbering interval: Specify the number of digits that the file numbering should use. So if it is set to 3, the files will be prepended by 001_, 002_ and so on.
gcode_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Line numbering interval: The interval which the line numbers will increase per line. So if it is 5 the line numbers will start at 5 and increase with 5 for each line, so the next line will be 10 and so on.

output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Output folder: Select the folder where generated G-code files will be saved.
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: File name: The name of the output G-code file(s) without extension.
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Name must be numeric: When enabled, program names will be required to be numeric.
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Prepend file sequence numb: Each file will be prepended with their index number according to the order of the browser. This is to make sure that the order of the setups or operations is kept so that they won't overwrite each other if a different selection is made and the output isn't empty.
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Number of file digits: When prepending a file name with a number, this setting will make sure that the number of digits used for the prepended number is no less than specified here. So if this value is 3, the file names will all start with three digits and an underscore (_), so 001_, 002_ and so on will be prepended.
output_tab.TOOLTIP: Operations grouping: How to group the operations into output files
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Operations grouping:
Choose how operations are grouped into output files.

Single file: All operations are combined into a single G-code file. This option is only available if the origin of all setups are the same.
If the setups are rotated on the X-axis it also requires that the Rotate A-Axis between setups option is selected and that the X-axes of all the selected setups are parallel.
Group on setup: Each setup is output as a separate G-code file. This option is only available if there is multiple setups that will be processed.
Group on setup and tool: Operations are grouped by setup and tool, so each time the tool changes within a setup a new file is created.
None, one file per operation: Each operation is output as its own G-code file.

output_tab.TOOLTIP: Flatten the file structure: Do not create subfolders for setups and operations
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Flatten the file structure:
When enabled, all output files will be placed directly in the output folder without any subfolders.

The files will be named according to the full path of their setup and operation to avoid name conflicts, separated by an underscore (_).
output_tab.TOOLTIP: Combine operations using same t: Combine consecutive operations using same tool
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Combine operations using s: Combine operations following each other that use the same tool into a single operation.
output_tab.TOOLTIP TEXT: Overwrite existing files: To allow overwriting already existing files this setting should be selected. Otherwise the plugin will stop the output when the first existing file is found.
